doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Lost gigs and work during Covid
summary: Cancelled shows and insurance for musicians, backyard gigs, and using time to work on piano and Levine's theory book.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: When is the last gig you played? Do you remember?
The last gig I played — I’ve played about four times since the end of February. And you know I used to play four times a week.

Oh yeah. And it’s awful. I was thinking about some of the guys that came to Jamey’s camp. A lot of those guys had contracts to do shows. Broadway shows. And they’re not doing anything. I was talking to a friend of mine the other day, the Indianapolis Symphony cancelled all the health insurance for all the orchestra members. So it’s just hard times man. I’ve never seen anything like this ever.

Oh yeah. Oh I did — a friend of mine we’ve been doing a string of shows outside in her backyard so I went down to play that. And then there was a guy that wants me to come up and do a jazz clinic in Minnesota, but you know you don’t even know if you’re going to have this stuff. You know JEN is supposed to be in Louisville. I don’t even know if they’re going to have JEN. So everything is kind of up in the air.
Definitely. Well let’s hope for the best and be positive, as you have said a number of times today.

Oh yeah. And this is really giving me a chance to kind of get my skill — it gives you a chance to kind of do some stuff that you wouldn’t necessarily have time to do because you were too busy doing other things.
So I’m trying to work on my piano chops and I’ve been going through Mark Levine’s Jazz Theory book for this class that I’ve been teaching, and trying to boost myself up.
